PF_STEPS|/notesF/overview: The data sheets set the working limits: substrate and air temperature 10–35 °C (10–30 °C for {V2260} and {V2370}), at least 3 °C above the dew point and a relative humidity of at most 80 % (65 % for {V360}); no water is added to the resins (except the prescribed dilution of {V360} and {V2260}); the pot lives (15–20 minutes for {SG3F}, 30 for {B351}, 35 for {GBM} and {SG3}, 40 for {V360}, 60 for {SG2} and {K4031}, 120 for {EV200}) and the overcoat windows are kept; the material is stored frost-free, cool and dry at 10–25 °C (12–24 months, {ANTI}, {FF}, {QS} and {R008} longer); opened containers are used promptly. The applicable safety data sheets, the GISCODE and the EMICODE of the products are observed.
PF_STEPS|/notesF/points/0: the ideal material temperature is +15 °C; the containers are brought to temperature before the work
PF_STEPS|/notesF/points/1: the mixing: component A stirred, component B added completely, approx. 3 minutes at approx. 300 rpm, decanted and stirred again
PF_STEPS|/notesF/points/2: the data sheets are the valid document: this guide follows the issues of 21/06/2023 – 14/05/2026
PF_STEPS|/notesF/points/3: a trial area where the substrate, the colour or the slip class are in doubt

PFS_T|/pfgarage/problem: The floor of a garage, a cellar or a small warehouse dusts under the tyres and the boxes, drinks the oil drip and the water the car brings in, stains and is never clean. The slab is dry and sound, the budget and the time are small — the floor must be done over a weekend and look finished.
PFS_T|/pfgarage/solution: The aqueous seal {V360} does the whole floor in two days: diluted with 8–10 % water as the primer, filled with {FF} for the pinholes and with quartz sand for the levelling, rolled criss-cross in two steps as the satin, pigmented, vapour-permeable seal — walkable after 16 hours, resistant to tyre softeners, heating oil, petrol and dilute acids. {ANTI} in the last step gives R10; the wall–floor joint is closed with {IPU}.
PFS_T|/pfwork/problem: A workshop, a laboratory, a sales or commercial unit: trolleys, tools, oils and cleaning agents on a dry concrete slab that must become a smooth, coloured, easy-to-clean floor — glossy in the showroom, slip resistant where it is washed — with the joints of the slab taken through and the anchor holes of the old machines filled.
PFS_T|/pfwork/solution: The pore-sealing primer {GBM} (or {G1270}), sanded; a scratch coat where the slab is rough; the self-levelling coating {B351} at approx. 1 mm, de-aerated with the spiked roller — approx. 70 N/mm², Shore D approx. 72, Bfl-s1; the glossy PU top seal {V2260}, with {ANTI} for R11; the joints cut and filled with {IPU}, chamfered under vehicle traffic; holes and anchors with {K4031}.
PFS_T|/pfhall/problem: A production or logistics hall: forklifts and pallet trucks on small hard wheels, dropped pallets, pallet racking on anchors, the machine bases that must be grouted, the wet zone at the loading door — and a floor that is cleaned with the scrubber-drier every night. The coating must carry the point loads and the impacts for years.
PFS_T|/pfhall/solution: {GBM} in two steps, the second sanded, levels and seals the slab; the machine bases and the rail grouting with {EV200} (approx. 109 N/mm² after 7 days); the thick coat of {B351} filled 2 : 1 with quartz sand at approx. 2 mm; the slip-resistant finish — interspersing coat, quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm, top seal — for R11 to R12; the field and connection joints with {IPU}, 25 % total deformation, edges chamfered 45°.
PFS_T|/pfdamp/problem: The slab is young and will not dry in time, a basement floor stands on ground water, a floor has no vapour barrier: the residual moisture is above 4 CM-% and vapour presses from below — a standard primer would lift. The programme does not allow weeks of drying, and the floor must be coated like a dry floor afterwards.
PFS_T|/pfdamp/solution: The barrier primer {SG3} bonds to the matt damp concrete and blocks vapour and negative pressing water up to 3 bar in two coats, the second sanded; {SG3F} where only 3.5 hours between the coats can be spared; {SG3T} up the plinth and the wall and for the capillary-breaking mortar. On the sanded barrier the coating of {B351}, the slip-resistant finish and the joints with {IPU} follow as on any dry floor.
PFS_T|/pfoil/problem: A workshop or a machine hall whose concrete has drunk oil for decades: the oil rises through the capillaries, no primer bonds, every coating lifts. The surface is damp from the cleaning, the breakouts of the old machine bases are open — and the new floor must carry forklifts.
PFS_T|/pfoil/solution: After shot blasting the surface is cleaned with {R008} and hot water — sprayed, scrubbed until brownish, rinsed, vacuumed, repeated — and not dried off; the special primer {SG2} bonds to the damp, oil-free concrete and blocks capillary-rising oil and vapour (sd > 100 m) and water to 3 bar, sanded over the whole surface. Then the hall floor: breakouts and bases with {EV200}, the thick coat of {B351} with quartz sand, the slip-resistant finish, the joints with {IPU}.
PFS_T|/pfsewage/problem: The tanks, channels and digestion towers of a sewage treatment plant: sewage, sulphuric acid formed by the biogenic corrosion down to pH 0–1, sea water, the abrasion of the flow and the stray currents of the plant attack concrete and steel — the sheet piles, the gullies, the anchors. The coating must be chemically resistant, elastifying and closed on both materials.
PFS_T|/pfsewage/solution: The thixotropic barrier primer {SG3T} on floor and walls of the cementitious substrate; breakouts, gullies and anchors grouted with {EV200}, watertight to 5 bar; the sealing coating {V2370} in two layers in alternating colours — on steel blasted to Sa 2½ the first layer is the primer — exposure class XWW4 after DIN 19753, Shore A approx. 80, stray-current insulating; the movement joints with {IPU}, −40 to +80 °C.
